Measured complete-update time favors the candidate (mean 8.34 s vs 17.26 s), yet deadline_misses=35 and real_time_demonstrated=false in both: no real-time claim. Zero force-bound violation in either run does not exclude legal near-bound input. This supports the study hypothesis that the candidate improves joint holding while retaining reach. Pilot_numerical is scoped to a saved projected state and one 0.01 s held candidate-specific first command: the pending weight candidates (0.05, 0.1) reproduce reference endpoint error (8.164e-4 m) and speed (1.0624e-2 m/s) exactly, differing only in guidance objective (0.07606, 0.07614). Local endpoint speed is not full-task holding maximum, so full-task directional and speed ordering remain unresolved; I abstain rather than freeze an order. Diagnostic disposition is defer with recommendation_id=null. Candidate adoption is independent and, on the program-computed joint-acceptance result, selects the completed candidate. The pending batch remains pending; this interpretation neither changes nor filters it.
